transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

Well, I'm here because... um... well, I've been having a little trouble lately. It's a bit embarrassing to talk about, to be honest with you. At my age, you'd think I'd have these things figured out. But it's about my eating. 

I try to keep it under control, I really do. But what scares me most is that... well, once I start eating, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for more. Even while I’m sitting there telling myself, 'Tom, stop this right now,' I just can't seem to stop them. I know I should be able to manage myself better, and I'm so sorry if this sounds foolish. 

Am I explaining that okay, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Tom, when you find yourself eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot extra?

Oh, dear... well... I suppose I should just be completely honest with you, Doctor. I feel quite ashamed even admitting it, to be perfectly frank. But... yes. There are times, after I've eaten too much, where I... well, I go into the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. 

It's just... I get so terribly panicked, you see. And, um... I have also taken laxatives sometimes. Just because I get so frightened that all that food is just going to stay inside me. I know it's a dreadful thing to do, especially for a man my age, and I'm so sorry to even have to tell you that. I really should know better by now. 

I hope you don't think too poorly of me. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Tom, can you tell me how often these episodes of eating more than you intended happen, and whether they occur even when you're not feeling particularly hungry?

Well, um... I suppose it happens quite a bit, to be perfectly honest. Mostly on those afternoons when I'm just alone at the house. And, oh dear... you asked if I'm hungry. Half the time, my stomach isn't rumbling at all. I just wander into the kitchen to find a little something to pass the time, but... well, I want to be a good patient and give you the full picture, even if it's terribly embarrassing to admit. 

Once I start, it just spirals. On those afternoons alone, I can go through... oh, a whole loaf of bread, the peanut butter, a box of cookies, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then ice cream. All in one sitting. It's like I don't even really look up or realize what I'm doing until it's all gone. 

I know it sounds terribly gluttonous, especially for an old man who certainly doesn't need all that food. I'm so sorry if that sounds awful, I really am trying to do better. Am I giving you the right kind of information, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Tom, during these times when you're eating more than you meant to, do you feel like you're not in control of what or how much you're eating?

Yes, Doctor... um, I think I might have touched on this a little bit when I first came in, and I hope you don't mind me repeating myself. I don't want to waste your time. But... yes, that's exactly it. 

It's actually the part that scares me the absolute most. Once I take that first bite, it's like... well, like my hands just have a mind of their own. They just keep reaching and reaching for more food. And the whole time, I'm sitting there, and inside my head I'm practically shouting, 'Tom, stop this right now, you silly old fool!' But I just... I can't seem to make myself stop. 

I know a man of my age should have much better willpower than that. It's terribly embarrassing to admit that I can't even control my own hands when it comes to a box of cookies. I really am trying to be better about it, I promise you that. 

Does that... does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Tom, can you tell me if these episodes of eating this way ever interfere with your daily life—like affecting your mood, your relationships, or even your ability to get things done during the day?

Oh, dear... well... I suppose I should be honest, even though it's quite difficult to admit. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, really I don't, but... yes, it does affect things a bit. 

I used to be quite involved with my community garden group, you know. I loved it. But lately... well, I've sort of pulled away from them. And from family meals, too. It's just... I find myself either trying to plan my day around when I can have my... my time with the food, or I'm just so terribly ashamed afterward that I can't bear to face anyone. I worry constantly that someone might look at me and just *know* what I've been doing. 

I know it's silly for an old man to be hiding away like that, and I'm so sorry if it sounds like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I really should be stronger and just go see my friends and family. I'm trying to, I really am. Am I giving you too much detail, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need to know.
Tom, do you usually eat this way only when you're alone because you're embarrassed about others seeing you eat like this?

Oh... yes, Doctor. Yes, that's exactly it. I... I would never, ever want anyone to see me like that. 

I suppose I do make quite sure that the house is completely empty, and... well, I even close the blinds sometimes, just in case a neighbor might happen to glance in. It's just so terribly humiliating to think of anyone watching an old man gorge himself that way. I want people to think of me as a respectable gentleman, you know? Not... not someone who has no control over himself. 

I'm so sorry, I know it's probably very foolish to be so concerned about what others think at my age. I really should know better by now. I hope I'm not sounding too vain or silly... is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Tom, can you tell me if these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress even when they’re not happening, like worrying about them or feeling guilty for hours or even days afterward?

Oh, well... I suppose I do think about it sometimes, yes. But really, I try my best not to let it bother me too much. I mean, everyone has things they regret doing, don't they? 

I do feel a little bit guilty sometimes, maybe for an hour or so after... just because I know I shouldn't be wasting good food, especially at my age when I ought to know better. But I really wouldn't say it causes me a lot of distress for days on end. I try to just put it out of my mind and focus on being a good neighbor and keeping the house tidy. I don't want to make a big fuss over it. 

I hope that's alright to say, Doctor. I just don't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself all the time. I really do try to keep a positive attitude about things. Is that... is that helpful for your notes?
Tom, do you find yourself overly concerned about your weight or body shape, or have you noticed any significant changes in your weight because of these episodes?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose everyone thinks about their waistline a little bit as they get older, don't they? I mean, I certainly wouldn't say I'm *overly* concerned about it. I'm just an old man, after all, not a young fellow trying to impress anyone at the beach. 

I do try to keep myself looking presentable, of course. I want my suits to fit properly for church and things like that. But I wouldn't say I spend all my time worrying about my shape. And as for my weight... well, I haven't really noticed any big changes, to be honest. I don't weigh myself very often. I just sort of... go by how my trousers feel. 

I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression, Doctor. I just don't want to sound vain or obsessed with my looks at my age. I try to be sensible about it all. Does that make sense? Am I answering what you needed to know?
Tom, how often do these episodes of eating more than you intended happen—like how many times a week or month?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose I should just be completely honest with you, even if it's a bit hard to say. I've been keeping some little food logs, just to try and keep myself accountable and do the right thing, you know? 

And... well, looking at them, it seems that for many months now, nearly every week has had at least one afternoon where I just... ate completely out of control. 

And then, of course, I feel I have to make up for it right away. To fix my mistake, so to speak. I'll try fasting, or really pushing myself extra hard with my walking and all my daily chores around the house, just to burn it off. And... well, sometimes... I'm so terribly embarrassed to admit this... I've even resorted to taking laxatives or making myself vomit. 

It sounds so undignified for a man my age, doesn't it? I know I shouldn't do those things, and I really am trying my best to be good, I promise you. I hope you don't think too badly of me for it. Is that... is that the sort of detail you needed for your records, Doctor?

Tom, can you describe what goes through your mind just before or during these episodes—specifically, do you feel like you’re making a choice to eat or does it feel like something you can’t stop yourself from doing, even if you want to?

Oh, goodness... that's a difficult question, isn't it? I suppose... well, I really do try to make good choices. I don't want you to think I'm just deliberately being greedy or foolish. I know right from wrong, certainly. 

But... oh, it's so hard to explain without sounding completely ridiculous. What scares me most—and I really am quite ashamed to admit this—is that once I start, it feels like... like my hands just keep reaching for more. Even while I'm sitting there, in my own kitchen, telling myself, "Tom, stop this right now. You're making a mistake." It's as if I just... can't quite make myself listen. 

I know that sounds terrible, like I have no willpower at all. I promise I usually have very good self-control in every other part of my life. I've always prided myself on being a disciplined man. It's just... in those moments, it feels like something else takes over, just for a little while. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely unhinged, Doctor. I really am trying to be better about it. Is that... does that answer your question properly? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
